assessment: In this interesting report, the authors probe the correlative effect of paternal obesity on placental development. In the substantively revised manuscript, the authors provide solid epigenomic data arising from dietary differences in fat intake in the male, subsequent chromatin changes in sperm, and link these outcomes to transcriptomic changes in offspring placenta. These useful insights will be of interest to those studying the epigenetic transmission of germline changes in the next generation, and those studying the relationship to metabolic exposure in the parental generation to offspring.
